headline: power back up to £122/MWh; gas climbing again after a brief dip off a two-year high
commentary: UK power has pushed back up to £122.44/MWh, up 4.47% on the day. After gas set a roughly two-year high in late July and eased for a couple of days, prices have turned higher again — front-month NBP gas is back around 142 p/therm and power has followed it up. The forward curve stays elevated through the winter (gas contracts hold near 148–149 p/therm into Q1 2027) and only really softens from summer 2027 (Q3 27 around 93 p/therm). The recent dip proved brief and the market is climbing off it — which is the case for fixing the energy block for the term rather than riding a curve that keeps grinding higher.

gas.note: NBP gas futures eased for a couple of days off a two-year high, but have started climbing again; the curve stays elevated through winter, only softening by summer 2027.
